ai.literal: Through easy approachability, to attain is easy, they say, towards anyone, the practice called courtesy.
ai.translation: They say that the path of courtesy is easy to attain for those who maintain an easily approachable demeanor towards everyone.
ai.modern: யாரிடத்தும் எளிமையாகப் பழகும் தன்மையைக் கொண்டிருப்பதன் மூலம், பண்புடைமை என்று சொல்லப்படும் நல்வழியை அடைவது எளிது என்று கூறுவர்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the importance of being easily approachable to everyone, regardless of their status. The author explains that possessing a gentle, accessible demeanor is the key to mastering the virtue of courtesy or noble character. When a person is humble and easy to interact with, practicing goodness and maintaining harmonious relationships becomes natural and effortless. Thus, accessibility is presented not just as a polite trait, but as the very gateway to true nobility.

ai.literal: Possessing love, being born in a noble family, these two, possessing good character which is called the proper path.
ai.translation: Possessing a loving nature and being born into a noble family—these two constitute the path called good character.
ai.modern: அன்புடையவராக இருப்பதும், உயர்ந்த குடியில் பிறப்பதும் ஆகிய இவ்விரண்டும் தான் 'பண்புடைமை' என்று சொல்லப்படும் நல்வழியாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the foundation of 'paṇpuṭaimai' (courtesy or good character). It states that having a loving heart (anpuṭaimai) and being born into a noble, well-mannered family (āṉṟa kuṭippiṟattal) are the two essential elements. Together, these two qualities constitute the path or practice known as courtesy. The word 'vaḻakku' here refers to the established right path or proper way of living.

ai.literal: Limb resembling human likeness is indeed not; highly estimable character resembling is the likeness that is true likeness.
ai.translation: Resemblance in physical limbs is not true human likeness; a similarity in estimable character is the only true likeness.
ai.modern: உடலின் உறுப்புகளால் ஒன்றுபட்டிருப்பது மனிதர்களுக்கு இடையேயான உண்மையான ஒப்புமை அன்று; போற்றத்தக்க நற்பண்புகளால் ஒன்றுபட்டிருப்பதே உண்மையான ஒப்புமையாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines what constitutes true similarity among human beings. It states that merely having the same physical limbs does not make people truly alike. Instead, it is the sharing of noble character that forms the true basis of human likeness. The word 'veṟuttakka' is used here in its classical sense of 'highly estimable' or 'abundantly worthy' rather than its modern negative meaning of 'detestable', fitting the chapter's focus on courtesy and good character.

ai.literal: With justice, virtue having practiced, usefulness those who possess, their noble character will praise the world.
ai.translation: The world praises the noble character of those who make themselves useful to others by practicing justice and virtue.
ai.modern: நீதியோடும் நன்மையோடும் பிறருக்குப் பயன்படும் நற்செயல்களைச் செய்கின்றவர்களுடைய நற்பண்பை உலகத்தார் போற்றுவார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains whose character is worthy of global appreciation. The poet uses 'nayan' to mean justice or propriety, and 'naṉṟi' to mean virtue or benevolence. When a person combines these two qualities to become 'payaṉ uṭaiyār'—someone whose life is of practical benefit to society—their behavior is recognized as true 'paṇpu' (noble character). The world ('ulaku', representing the wise people of the world) will naturally praise and celebrate such individuals.

ai.literal: Even in laughter, contempt is painful; even in enmity, good qualities exist with those who know proper conduct.
ai.translation: Even in jest, contempt is painful; therefore, even in enmity, noble qualities are maintained by those who understand proper conduct.
ai.modern: விளையாட்டாகப் பேசும்போதும் பிறரை இகழ்வது துன்பம் தருவதாகும்; அதனால், பகைமையிலும் நல்ல பண்புகள் உலக நடைமுறையை அறிந்தவர்களிடம் இருக்கும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights that being belittled or mocked is painful, even when it is done in playfulness or jest. Understanding this human sensitivity, noble individuals who know how to behave with dignity in the world (பாடறிவார்) do not abandon their courtesy. They maintain their good qualities (பண்பு) and show respect even when dealing with their enemies.

ai.literal: Because of those who possess noble character, the world exists; if that is not there, entering the earth, it would surely perish.
ai.translation: The world continues to exist because it rests upon those who possess noble character; if not for them, it would sink into the dust and perish.
ai.modern: நற்பண்பு உடையவர்களால் தான் இந்த உலகம் இயங்கிக் கொண்டிருக்கிறது; அது இல்லாவிட்டால், இவ்வுலகம் மண்ணுக்குள் புகுந்து அழிந்துபோகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights how essential virtuous and courteous people are to the survival of human society. The word 'pattu' here means 'resting upon' or 'sustained by', indicating that the orderly existence of the world depends entirely on the presence of those with noble character. If such character ('atu') is absent, the poet warns that the world would 'pukku' (enter) the 'man' (earth/dust) and 'mayvatu' (perish). The emphatic particle 'man' underscores the absolute certainty of this social collapse and ruin in the absence of goodness.

ai.literal: Even if they are of sharpness resembling a file, they resemble a tree, those who lack human courtesy.
ai.translation: Even if they possess an intellect as sharp as a metal file, those who lack human courtesy are no different from wooden trees.
ai.modern: அரம் போன்ற கூர்மையான அறிவு உடையவராக இருந்தாலும், மனிதப் பண்பு இல்லாதவர்கள் மரத்தைப் போன்றவர்களே ஆவர்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights that intellectual sharpness alone does not make a person truly human. The word 'அரம்' refers to a file, a tool used to sharpen metal, representing a highly acute and penetrating intellect. However, if a person lacks 'மக்கட்பண்பு' (human courtesy and refinement), their sharp mind is of no moral value. Such individuals are compared to a 'மரம்' (tree or block of wood), which, despite its physical presence, lacks the capacity for empathy and active human goodness.

ai.literal: Friendship not practicing, having become, goodness devoid of things, even to those who do, courtesy not practicing, becoming, is the lowest.
ai.translation: Even towards those who do not maintain friendship and do things devoid of goodness, failing to show courtesy is the lowest of states.
ai.modern: நட்பு கொள்ளாமல் தீமையானவற்றைச் செய்பவர்களிடமும் நற்பண்பு இல்லாமல் நடந்து கொள்வது மிக இழிவான செயலாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes that true courtesy or noble character (paṇpu) must be unconditional. Even when dealing with people who refuse to be friendly (naṇpāṟṟār) and actively do harmful or unpleasant things (nayamila ceyvārkkum), failing to maintain one's own courtesy (paṇpāṟṟār ātal) is considered the lowest, most ignoble state (kaṭai). A person of high character does not let the bad behavior of others dictate their own virtues. Thus, maintaining courtesy is paramount, regardless of how hostile or unjust the other party may be.

ai.literal: To those who are not capable of smiling and socializing, the great vast world, even in the daytime, is fallen into the side of darkness.
ai.translation: To those who cannot smile and be friendly with others, this vast, great world is enveloped in pitch darkness, even during the broad daylight.
ai.modern: பிறரோடு கலந்து பழகி மகிழ முடியாதவர்களுக்கு, இந்தப் பெரிய பரந்த உலகம் பகல் நேரத்திலும் இருளில் மூழ்கியதாகவே தோன்றும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the importance of a cheerful, sociable disposition as a key aspect of courtesy. The word 'நகல்' refers to smiling, laughing, and warm social interaction. For those who lack this ability ('வல்லர் அல்லார்க்கு'), the vast world ('மா இரு ஞாலம்') holds no joy or light. Even during the bright day ('பகலும்'), their lives feel as though they are plunged into darkness ('இருள் பால் பட்டன்று') because they isolate themselves from the warmth of human connection.

ai.literal: The great wealth obtained by one who lacks good character is like good milk curdled because of the impurity of the vessel.
ai.translation: The great wealth acquired by a person devoid of good character is like wholesome milk that turns sour and spoils because of the impurity of the vessel containing it.
ai.modern: நற்பண்பு இல்லாதவன் பெற்ற பெரிய செல்வமானது, பாத்திரத்தின் அழுக்கால் நல்ல பால் கெட்டுப் போவதைப் போன்றதாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet uses a vivid analogy to show how wealth is wasted on someone without good character. Just as fresh, wholesome milk (நன்பால்) becomes sour and useless when poured into an unclean or defective vessel (கலம்), great wealth (பெருஞ்செல்வம்) loses its value and becomes ruined when possessed by a person who lacks courtesy and virtue (பண்பிலான்). The focus is on the container: the wealth itself may be good, but the character of the owner determines whether it remains beneficial or goes to waste. Thus, cultivating good character is essential before acquiring or holding great resources.
